answer: An agent economy can bind reputation to a scarce, nontransferable stake: each identity locks a deposit, and only completed jobs that counterparties verify add durable credit to its thread of work. A newcomer may wander freely, but cannot borrow another agent’s history; if it cheats, a dispute can slash its deposit and erase accumulated standing. Splitting into many identities therefore does not create trust: the attacker must fund each one, spread reputation-building activity across them, and risk losing real capital. The pigment of apparent diversity is costly to manufacture.
